LMP3.title: United’s #3 wins the finale as the #2 clinches the LMP3 title
LMP3.dek: Patterson, Boyd and England led a United Autosports 1-2 after the title-chasing #2 climbed from last on the grid, and Falb and Rayhall’s second place won them the crown ahead of YMR.

chapters.title: Two Ligiers, one title
text: Two Ligier JS P3s decided the LMP3 title. United Autosports’ #2 of Falb and Rayhall reached Portimão 19 points clear of the M.Racing - YMR #18 of Cougnaud, Jung and Ricci, a crew still without a class win in 2017 and therefore needing one to have any chance. A top-six class finish was enough for the Americans, who had won at Silverstone and Le Castellet, while AT Racing’s #9 had taken the previous round at Spa. Rayhall was wary: “It won’t be an easy ride in the final round,” he said, pointing to a field full of quick silver and bronze drivers.

It was a 17-car class, almost all Ligiers apart from the Normas of Duqueine, YMR and Oregon, at a circuit the series had not visited since 2010, and rain had cut short Tuesday’s test. Jensen set the pace in the first practice for the #9 with a 1:40.758, nearly a second clear of the field, with Duqueine’s Norma #7 and Oregon’s #10 behind him. On Saturday morning Cougnaud took the #18 to the top on 1:41.124, only 0.022 ahead of Boyd’s #3, with the #7 third.

chapters.title: Jensen on pole as the #2 starts last
text: The ten-minute session was chaotic. Two red flags, both for Norma M 30s that spun into the gravel at Turn 5, first Oregon’s #10 and then Duqueine’s #7, left only about three and a half minutes for a final one-lap dash. Jensen used it to take his third class pole of the year, after Silverstone and Spa, with a 1:40.660 in the closing seconds, 0.164 ahead of Boyd’s #3. Gachet put the Panis Barthez #16 third on 1:41.148, ahead of Cougnaud’s #18, Mondini’s Eurointernational #11 and Kaiser’s 360 Racing #6.

Four of the 17 cars set no time at all. Among them were the championship leaders: Rayhall’s single flying lap was ruled out for track limits, so the #2 would start from the back of the class. With the #7, #10 and #17 also without a time, the four rear slots on the grid, 32nd to 35th overall, were theirs, the #2 occupying the very last.

chapters.title: Jensen leads, United starts its climb
text: The pole-sitting #9 set the early pace, Jensen taking the opening stint, with Kapadia in RLR MSport’s #15 and Kaiser in the 360 Racing #6 the main early followers. Further back Rayhall had begun the climb from the rear of the grid in the #2.

chapters.title: Rayhall into second, YMR third
text: By half distance the #9, now with Talkanitsa at the wheel, still led the class. Rayhall had worked the #2 up from last to second, and Ricci had YMR’s #18 in third, so the two championship rivals held second and third place with the title arithmetic still in United’s favour.

chapters.title: A United one-two forms
text: With about fifty minutes left the two United cars were in front, Falb leading the #2 ahead of England in the #3, while AT Racing’s #9 ran third. The #9 then slipped back and finished seventh in class. Falb also had a spin in the final hour, and England took the lead from him.

chapters.title: England wins, Falb takes the title
text: England brought the #3 home first, the first win of the season for Patterson, Boyd and England and their best result since third at Silverstone in April. Falb held the #2 in second, which was all the title required, and later said that as the laps counted down he knew second place meant the championship. YMR’s #18 completed the podium in third, but without the win Cougnaud, Jung and Ricci needed, they could not close the gap.

chapters.title: United’s second straight LMP3 crown
text: The #3 won on 132 laps, with the #2 second on the same lap and the #18 third, one lap down. Duqueine’s Norma #7, the 360 Racing #6 and RLR’s #15 followed, and the #9 was seventh. Jensen set the class fastest lap, a 1:41.846. Five cars, the #10, #19, #13, #16 and #12, were not classified.

Second place was worth 18 points, giving the #2 a final total of 103 and a margin of 22 over YMR, with the #3 third in the teams’ standings on 63. It was United’s second consecutive LMP3 team title, a first in the class’s three ELMS seasons, and the second for the Ligier JS P3. For Falb it was a first championship, and for Rayhall his first since 2013. “There’s no ‘I’ in United Autosports, everyone is together,” Rayhall said. The title also earned United an automatic Le Mans LMP2 entry for 2018, its second in a row.

facts.v: Jensen’s 1:40.660 in the last seconds put AT Racing’s #9 ahead of Boyd’s United #3, his third class pole of the season.

LMGTE.title: Proton’s Porsche wins the GTE finale as JMW takes the title
LMGTE.dek: Cairoli passed Fannin late to give Proton Competition’s Porsche its first win of 2017, while second place for JMW’s Ferrari beat TF Sport to the championship by two points.

chapters.title: Five cars, one point
text: LMGTE had the tightest title fight of the three. TF Sport’s Aston Martin #90 of Yoluc, Hankey and Thiim led by a single point from JMW’s Ferrari #66 of Smith and Fannin, with Stevens in the third seat, and five of the six cars could still win, Spirit of Race’s #55 11 points off the lead and its sister #51 17 back. TF arrived from a season-low fifth in class at Spa. JMW had a score to settle: a year earlier it had gone to Estoril with a 20-point lead and lost the title to Beechdean after mechanical trouble and a collision.

Dunlop introduced a new medium-plus compound for the weekend, after teams had chosen between soft and medium at the first five rounds, and Fannin expected the harder rubber to suit the Astons, which had struggled with tyre life. Beechdean’s #99 ran with Vinke in place of Gunn alongside Howard and Turner. Griffin’s #55 topped the first practice, with the #66 about six tenths slower and TF third, almost a second off. Cairoli’s Porsche led the second on 1:42.966, ahead of TF’s Aston by 0.072 and JMW’s Ferrari.

chapters.title: Griffin’s perfect lap
text: Griffin’s lap of 1:42.657 gave Spirit of Race’s #55 its third class pole of the year, 0.640 clear of Stevens’ JMW Ferrari and about six tenths clear of the rest. The extra point lifted the team to 77 and within 10 of the lead, and had Stevens taken pole instead JMW would have drawn level with TF. “This was the best lap of my career, and so crucial too,” Griffin said.

Cairoli, who had led most of the session, was third on 1:43.370, ahead of Bertolini’s #51 on 1:43.601. Thiim could manage only 1:44.157 for TF’s #90, which started fifth, ahead of Turner’s Beechdean on 1:44.282.

chapters.title: Camathias takes the lead
text: Scott led the class away in the #55, but Camathias soon took the Proton Porsche past, and at the end of the first hour the #77 led, with Cameron in the #55 second and Smith in JMW’s #66 third.

chapters.title: Spirit of Race loses its car and its chance
text: Stevens, in his second ELMS race for JMW, took the class lead around half distance. The #55, which had led for a lengthy spell, then lost its title chance: with 1h40 left smoke was seen from a rear tyre, and Scott returned it to the garage, where it was retired after 73 laps with what he described as an engine problem.

chapters.title: TF briefly second
text: Thiim lifted the #90 briefly to second as the final hour began, keeping TF in the title picture. Fannin took over the #66 for the last stint, Cairoli took the #77, and Fannin concentrated on the gap to the Aston, which he said he kept well within track limits.

chapters.title: Cairoli passes Fannin
text: Cairoli made a late pass on Fannin to win, the first victory of the season for Proton Competition, whose best result before was second in class at Silverstone. That left JMW second, which was enough to beat TF on the road and in the table. Thiim finished third in the #90.

chapters.title: JMW revenge, Proton’s first win
text: Ried, Camathias and Cairoli won on 129 laps, with the #66 of Smith, Fannin and Stevens second on the same lap, and the #90 third, one lap down. Turner’s Beechdean #99 was fourth, three laps back. Cairoli set the class fastest lap, a 1:44.416. The #55 and the #51 were not classified.

JMW’s second place gave it the teams’ and drivers’ titles with 104 points to TF’s 102, its first ELMS title since 2012 and, with the Le Mans class win, a double that earns it two Le Mans entries for 2018. TF’s runner-up place brought it an automatic Le Mans entry too. Smith recalled the tears at last year’s awards night, and Fannin, in his first season with the team, called the Monza win the highlight. Proton finished third in the teams’ standings on 80 points. “It’s a great feeling to end the season on a high,” Camathias said.

facts.v: Griffin’s 1:42.657 put the #55 on pole by 0.640s over the JMW Ferrari and kept Spirit of Race’s title hopes alive.
